questions.prompt: Line ℓ is the perpendicular bisector of segment AB, meeting AB at M. Point P is on ℓ. Prove that PA = PB.
questions.prompt_markup: Line ℓ is the perpendicular bisector of segment AB, meeting AB at M. Point P is on ℓ. Prove that PA = PB.
questions.required_method: Use SAS on triangles PMA and PMB.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: AM = BM (M is the midpoint); ∠PMA ≅ ∠PMB (both right angles, ℓ ⊥ AB); PM = PM (reflexive); △PMA ≅ △PMB (SAS); PA = PB (corresponding parts). If P = M, PA = MA = MB = PB directly. Alternative: the reflection across ℓ fixes P and swaps A and B.

questions.correct_answer: PM ⊥ AB, so P is on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.required_method: Use SSS on triangles PMA and PMB, then the linear pair of congruent angles at M.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). questions.prompt: In a coordinate plane, A(-a, 0) and B(a, 0) with a > 0. Prove that every point P(0, y) on the y-axis is equidistant from A and B, and that every point P(x, y) with PA = PB has x = 0.
questions.prompt_markup: In a coordinate plane, A(-a, 0) and B(a, 0) with a > 0. Prove that every point P(0, y) on the y-axis is equidistant from A and B, and that every point P(x, y) with PA = PB has x = 0.
questions.correct_answer: PA = PB = √(a² + y²) for P(0, y); and PA = PB gives (x + a)² = (x - a)², so x = 0.
questions.required_method: Use the distance formula in both directions.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: both directions. (1) √(a² + y²) both ways. (2) (x + a)² + y² = (x - a)² + y² simplifies to 4ax = 0, and a ≠ 0, so x = 0.
